Ryug is the collective name for the Fourth Generation people. Improved from the five primal races, the Third Generation, they call themselves perfect beings. They hold a power unlike any weapon or magic before, and those whose power leans toward protection are called Shield Ryug.

If those strong at protecting themselves are called Shield Ryug, those strong at healing others are called Healer Ryug. Healer Ryug are said to have the power to instantly heal not only outward wounds but even wounds of the heart.

Those with extremely strong power to attack foes are called Destroyer Ryug. It's said that when Ryug of shield, healing and destruction appear together, anyone of any power will bow down, so Ryug prefer to act in threes when they can.

A Fourth Generation Ryug man, recommended by Void, god of subspace, and sent to Elminage as a next-librarian candidate. Gifted even among gifted Ryug, Hevayur believes his own race will find the Eld, so he loathes those failures, the giants, dragons and five races, and takes being ranked with them as an insult.

Hisbert's last duty: naming Hevayur for the next term. The vote: Aznand 2, Hevayur 4, Zoni 1. The expected runoff never came; next is Hevayur. Behind a relieved Void, Fulfaray's heartless smile.

The poster girl of the tavern in Algrantz. A bright, ever-smiling girl who makes friends with anyone. Her flaw is a sloppy memory: she brings something other than what was ordered and soon forgets what she's told. But once they see her smile, everyone forgives her: "Oh, well."

An old dragonewt who has run an inn in Algrantz for years. Lazy, he hates making beds and preparing for guests, so he puts adventurer after adventurer in the no-fuss stable. Since his wife, who kept him in line, passed away, his sloth has grown. Some adventurers resist, but most bow to his brute strength.

The woman who owns Kembeck's Shop. She first ran it with her adventurer husband. Nights spent appraising the goods he brought home left her with a hard glare. Though he has passed away, she still keeps the shop full of memories. Her son has a shop in Roscadil.

A young bishop with a keen head for business. He openly craves money, rank and fame, all that clergy (at least outwardly) hold taboo. When he sees an injured adventurer, he can't help seeing money. His dream is to build a temple bearing his own name. Go for it, Hardy the philistine!
King of Algrantz. He calls himself a wartime king and leaves all but military matters to trusted vassals. He is foul-mouthed and tiresome, but that seems to be his way of communicating.

As she won renown as an adventurer, Balgert spotted and hired her for the Training Hall. Polite and caring, she overuses sound effects like "Zubabaan!" in lessons, so she's a bit cryptic. Her sword pupils are easy to spot, as the habit rubs off; it has even leapt the Hall to a girl at a certain tavern.

A man who enjoys tea time in a corner of Wells Garden from sunrise to sunset. He is in fact the Executor of the Roscadil Empire. Without his approval, no one may meet Her Majesty. Every day, they say, adventurers and notables bearing sweets and tea form a long line to see him.

The gardener of Wells Garden. In his hands, plants grow lush and lovely as works of art. Lately he found a sapling that talks noisily. It begs to be planted soon, yet gripes endlessly: "I want somewhere wetter," "Not enough sun." Even he seems fed up.

The lead developer of the magic airship. Madulay holds that "technology is meant to save people, not to kill them," and is not keen on building the airship, a warship. Yet, trusting Rianna, Madulay pours everything into finishing the airship again today.

A swordmaster who mastered the secret arts. She honed her blade traveling from city to city, then one day suddenly lost interest in everything, gave up the sword and took up philosophy. She takes pupils on a whim, but her extreme hands-off style earns only bad press. Her most recent pupil is Milonya.

The only son of Gia of Kembeck's Shop. Excitement-loving Toner learned reading, writing and sums, then promptly begged Gia for a little shop in Roscadil. Word of the little shopkeeper spread fast, and before long the shop was one of Roscadil's famous stores, even stocking the knights' surplus gear.

A girl who appears when Toner's curiosity peaks and a rainbow of excitement envelops Toner's body. Peek into Toner's Armory at night after closing, and you may see the shopkeeper leaping about, swinging a rod and shouting "Sanafeet Death Motion!"

Empress of Roscadil. As if driven, she pushes mana furnace research, and lost half her body in a failed test. Barred from the site since, she won't listen. Unless she draws power from the furnace every two days, half her body won't move, they say. She loathes crude Balgert and the nature-loving, useless ogres.

A girl swordfighter whose splendid beard is adorable. She tore it off Shimerief as a graduation keepsake. Something else was supposed to be given, but Milonya had her eye on that beard all along; she may even have become a pupil just for it. Smitten with Decoy at first sight, she can't hide her lust.

A Magic Puppet full of interest in humans ever since an alchemist made it. It pesters humans and dumps trouble on them. Its pranks sometimes go too far, but a real scolding leaves Decoy crestfallen, repenting in the shade of a tree. Maybe it's just lonely, after all. It finds Milonya physically repulsive.

An old goblin who runs a magic shop in Lumisthenes. Goblins and ogres form closed societies, so much knowledge stays buried within them. Seeing that as a loss of knowledge, Lotz came to Lumisthenes to put his own to use. Through his knowledge, people learn new sides of the land.

A Temple of Rafa fortune-teller. Skilled, but so addicted to gambling she's called "Lumisthenes' Disgrace." Up late at the casino, she often dozes off during day readings. Out of food money, she borrows from those around her, Mayleen first. She even owes Wattner some. Truly hopeless.

Lumisthenes has a temple to Rafa, so it is naturally seen as the land's center. When matters affect the land, it hosts the Central Council of rulers from all over, chaired by Wattner. Wattner puts the land first, and perhaps for that reason sees things a bit differently from the other rulers.

Keeper of the Stargazing Lighthouse, a celestial observatory. When young, she caused a ruckus after adventurers teased her; Wattner rebuked her, and she lost her real post. She won back trust over years, but came to hate adventurers for it, and resents that her job forces her to deal with them.

A woman called the Queen of Opera. Her fine voice began to shine in nursery school. In early childhood she was already called "the Goddess's Voice" and cheered everywhere. Her musical learning is said to be court-orchestra class. She owes her fine education, they say, to someone backing her from the shadows...

An ogre woman who raids food stalls in Teridon. She dines and dashes so brazenly that owner after owner is left stunned or gives up as if it were a passing shower (strictly, she doesn't even run, so she eats and strolls). But a nuisance has arisen to rebuke her: Molder.

Teridon's Captain of the Guard. Guards in name, nearly vigilantes in fact. With a strong sense of justice, Molder misses no wrong, however small, and shuns force, urging reform by talk. Sounds weak? Being lectured head-on, a finger pointed so close you can see its prints, is tough on the mind.

The chief who holds real power in Teridon. Not a king, but Barjeff's vast wealth controls most goods flowing in Teridon and across the land. So no nation can ignore Barjeff, who is often called to the continent's Central Council. Barjeff lives by the motto of love and forces it on everyone in sight.

A werebeast girl with elephant traits who works at the Love Jacuzzi. Like an elephant, she can scoop up water and shower it from her trunk. Teridon's chief Barjeff dotes on her, but to her, Barjeff is just a pushover "uncle" who gives her pocket money.
A Devilish woman. Despite her alluring body, Yuna is a pure, modest woman. She always gently reins in the bold Nora. Their exchanges are popular with some customers.

One of the deputy librarians, reluctantly left minding the Elminage System on Hisbert's orders. He has no interest in the librarian's overreach, Hevayur's rise or the missing Zoni. His steady work has some calling him Hevayur's rival.

A vampire who counsels people burdened with feelings beyond saving. She talks deeply with those who wish to die, and only if they still wish it does she quietly end their lives with her fangs. Her fangs hold a strange power: lives taken by her bite are said never to stray from the Path of Souls.

A girl in Perpeco Village. For some reason she was abandoned in a basket near the forest with an Arob, and they were raised like siblings. Her big brother the Arob (or rather, Anib) understands human speech and bravely defended the village when monsters attacked. Bona is proud of great Anib.

A werebeast thief. A life of self-reliance gave Brassel very strong willpower, but also no patience for others' softness, so Brassel can be a little hard to approach. Brassel formed a thieves' gang and leads the other thieves as its boss.

The trusty boss of the ogres and goblins. Not the sharpest mind, but Fulgrant's flashes of inspiration are not to be underestimated. The goblins refine those flashes, and the ogres give them form. That, it seems, is how Ogre Bay runs.

Daughter of the wicked mage who raided an Ice Magic Seal temple somewhere; a cursed child of the mage's lustful assault on a spirit. Heir to both the evil, mighty mage and the spirit, the land's blessing, she became a rare mage. As a child she had no place and stayed at Deltoi, and knows its concealing art.

A Demon Duke called Radiance, who rose from the Wastelands seeking true justice. Though a Demon Duke, she holds the Radiant Scales, an Argument for choosing librarians. She is said to have some tie to the current librarian Hisbert, and her moves are watched closely.
A mysterious woman traveling the land. Her origins are unknown, and much about her is strange, such as never parting with her Mirage Cloak. Who could she be?

The fairy king who rules Nertowayu, which broke away from Nertowa in the Castle of the Wind. Meem seems to know Rafa the Sun Spirit and Yorfa the Moonlight Spirit well, but Meem's lips stay firmly sealed.

A dragon living since ancient times in the old cloud castle called the Castle of the Wind. Very long-lived, Agintaitus watched with Zaalhaut as Rafa the Sun Spirit ascended to the Palace of the Sun. Agintaitus seems to know Hisbert...?

An info broker who trades all over while gathering information. Hanoi misses no tale, however trivial; it's no stretch to call that store of info the continent's best. Hanoi's home is said to be in Perpeco Village, but Hanoi rarely returns. Inside, papers of info gathered so far are stacked to the ceiling.

A follower of the Demon Duke Hilde, though not a very loyal one. Once an undead thing of nothing but bones, Makakuri traveled in search of a body of flesh and blood. With that goal achieved, Makakuri now only gets moving, grudgingly, when Ruu nags. Lazy, and quick to run away.

A follower of the Demon Duke Hilde. Under the law of the Wastelands, where the weak are culled, she lost her place in the world, and she has sworn loyalty to Hilde, who gave her a safe haven. This time she has been asked to search for a certain woman. But who could that be?
A tiger lord of majestic bearing. Mandelgius was apparently roaming the land for some purpose with a friend named Rondelgius, but the two got separated along the way.

A Valkyrie girl. She once guarded the Temple of Rafa, but her habit of doing things at her own pace led to failure after failure, and she was thrown out. Since then, she seems to be scraping by as an adventurer.
A girl raised in the Perpeco Forest. An alchemist, she came to Algrantz seeking the money and know-how to rebuild her village, which was attacked by monsters.
A unicorn who has been with Electra since they were both little. Having always eaten and slept alongside people, Mig is convinced of deserving the same treatment as any human.

An adventurer working as a bounty hunter. Yamuru teamed up with Electra because they shared the same interest: making money. Lately, though, Electra has been holding Yamuru back, and with the bounty hunting so inefficient, Yamuru has begun to wonder if going solo would be better.

A girl fascinated by the legends of the Moonlight Spirit. Puzzled that there are so many legends of the Sun Spirit and almost none of the Moonlight Spirit, she set out to find them herself. Caught in a trap and unable to move, she was rescued by Yamuru, and has traveled with Yamuru ever since.

An old bishop who lay collapsed after a monster attack until Electra came to the rescue. Partly out of gratitude, Korbitz now travels with Electra, meaning to spend the years left supporting someone so accident-prone. Korbitz thinks of Electra as a grandchild and holds Electra very dear.

Mokero ran with a gang of thieves in the Crotoa City Ruins, but after attacking Electra's party, got beaten back, was lectured by Electra and turned over a new leaf. Ever since, Mokero has called Electra 'Miss' and has been with Electra's party, putting skills from those thieving days to use.

God of death, ruling the end of life. Though young, this god grasps life and death deeply, fit to be the last hope of the Divine Realm. Grieving over, cherishing and accepting a body of both sexes, the young god... will the Path of Souls be repaired?

Tiny Reckdas look-alikes emerging from deep in the fog Reckdas gives off. Don't drop your guard because they're small or mere illusions. The land's common sense doesn't apply to Demon Dukes. Treat each as the Demon Duke in person, only smaller, or countless Petit-Das will swarm you, leaving you a pitiful sight.

A beastfolk of bizarre appearance.
On first meeting, all are shocked by... First?
Perhaps you have met him before. He has come back here now, far more powerful than he ever was. Whether you knew him before or are seeing him for the first time, you would do well to be very careful.

The grand professor who takes on challengers at the Magical Party! With a whistle in the mouth, the prof will tweet-tweet everyone's magic away! Show off your amazing magic and maybe you'll get something good~!? Prof. Rombino is the prof's half-sibling: same mother, different father!

The grand professor who takes on challengers at the Martial Arts Tourney, rating everyone's attacks with a wave of a war fan~! Physical attacks can't kill the prof, but really strong ones still seem to be a weak spot. Don't bully the prof too much, okay?
A girl raised in the Perpeco Forest. An alchemist, she came to Algrantz seeking the money and know-how to rebuild her village, which was attacked by monsters.
A unicorn who has been with Electra since they were both little. Having always eaten and slept alongside people, Mig is convinced of deserving the same treatment as any human.

An adventurer working as a bounty hunter. Yamuru teamed up with Electra because they shared the same interest: making money. Lately, though, Electra has been holding Yamuru back, and with the bounty hunting so inefficient, Yamuru has begun to wonder if going solo would be better.

A girl fascinated by the legends of the Moonlight Spirit. Puzzled that there are so many legends of the Sun Spirit and almost none of the Moonlight Spirit, she set out to find them herself. Caught in a trap and unable to move, she was rescued by Yamuru, and has traveled with Yamuru ever since.

An old bishop who lay collapsed after a monster attack until Electra came to the rescue. Partly out of gratitude, Korbitz now travels with Electra, meaning to spend the years left supporting someone so accident-prone. Korbitz thinks of Electra as a grandchild and holds Electra very dear.

Mokero ran with a gang of thieves in the Crotoa City Ruins, but after attacking Electra's party, got beaten back, was lectured by Electra and turned over a new leaf. Ever since, Mokero has called Electra 'Miss' and has been with Electra's party, putting skills from those thieving days to use.
